newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.8 pct in Jan - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.8 pct in Jan - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.8 percent in the first four weeks of fiscal January versus December, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 6.5 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales advanced 6.7 percent in the week ended February 1 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
Sales performance was softer from the previous week, but not sufficiently to prevent a strong end to the fiscal month, the report said.
"(Sales) in the last two weeks were quite strong," said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.
A "well-balanced" economy coupled with strong consumer confidence and "benign" winter weather in the Northeast helped overall sales, Eilenberg said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.

Eilenberg said strong consumer confidence is being driven by a robust economy. "There is a correlation there between employment, income and consumer confidence, and that's in pretty good shape," he said.
He noted many stores are gearing up for the spring season, but many are still clearing out winter inventory by offering clearance sales.
Turning to volume versus profit, Eilenberg said 1996 will bea good profit year for retailers.

Although retailers did not run as many promotions in 1996 as they did in previous years, "overall you are going to see better profits when the profit statements come out in a couple of weeks," he added.
